What improved, and what did not

Temporal, channel-shared EEG features and training-derived sequence smoothing improved stage kappa and macro-F1 on the original BOAS test people. Because v1 results had already been inspected, this is a development comparison. The released Bitbrain comparator still leads.

EvaluationPeopleKappaSleep-time MAEGlobal / scaled range coverage

The primary external result uses every valid scored epoch in the complete recording. Its long daytime wake periods differ from the BOAS night window. The prespecified secondary sleep-window result is shown as secondary, not substituted for the primary failure.

Stage accuracy does not establish reliable sleep totals. V2 missed the 90% interval-coverage target. Per-person numerical prediction ranges remain research diagnostics in the data files; the interface does not release them as calibrated ranges.

Inspect frozen predictions

BOAS reference reveal also displays Bitbrain and v1 on the same time axis. YASA was not run; no curve is invented. On a small screen, scroll the plot horizontally. Unknown reference and unusable signals are gaps. Probabilities remain model estimates, not clinical safety scores.

Challenge a claim

Evaluation discipline

  • 48 fit people; six model-selection people; six separate probability-calibration people; 20 summary-calibration people. Repeat nights remain grouped.
  • Three sequence weights were compared only on six development people. No old test, summary-calibration or external labels selected the model.
  • Model, temperature, interval rules and cohort were frozen before opening external reference labels. Model checksum is recorded.
  • All 20 external signal/reference pairs match PhysioNet's published SHA-256 values. Fpz-Cz alone is resampled from 100 to 256 Hz using a fixed preprocessing rule.
  • R&K stages 3 and 4 map to N3. This reference differs from BOAS consensus scoring, so external results do not confirm identical-device performance.
  • Centered context uses neighbouring future epochs: this is offline retrospective inference.

No ADHD diagnosis, medication-response prediction, personalised gel choice, safe-dose recommendation or clinical validation is claimed.
